Executive verdict

The Pi captures are structurally intact and internally coherent. I found no evidence of missing bytes, odd-byte alignment shifts, word/channel shifts, duplicated 256-byte transport blocks, or rail-like bit-error spikes.

  • All 23 files are exactly 767,976 bytes. All match both the JSON sidecar SHA-256 and SHA256SUMS.
  • Every sidecar records exactly 767,997 UART bytes: 7-byte command echo + 767,976-byte ILD1 record + 14-byte completion/prompt. The omitted .wire.bin files were not independently re-hashed in this reduced archive.
  • All descriptors declare 31 frames × 36 chirps × 4 RX × 43 bins × complex IQ16, with correct 3,000 or 10,000 µs deltas.
  • Across 8,829,792 signed components, maximum magnitude is 17,330, with zero rail hits and 5.53 dB component headroom.
  • The P10 per-loop 12-channel complex fingerprint correlation never falls below 0.999582; a byte/word/channel slip would break this pattern immediately.

Limit: ILD1 v7 carries no on-device payload checksum. Host SHA-256 proves preservation after the Pi wrote the file, not the IWR-memory-to-Pi hop. The evidence is strong enough to trust these captures for engineering work, but only a firmware-generated CRC/sequence scheme can certify isolated low-order bit errors.

Baseline judgment

Use the 10 ms / 5-post profile for the next session. It delivered 10/10 full 767,976-byte captures, hwa_missed=0, matched freeze request/completion counters, and showed excellent 12-element amplitude/phase repeatability.

The 3 ms files themselves are clean, but hwa_missed increments once per dump. That makes P3 a weaker timing baseline even though it is not a UART corruption problem.

The present scene is useful as a transport/electronics baseline, not yet as the authoritative no-material reference. Bin 2 at 0.094 m dominates and is coupling/very-near-range energy. There is a weaker return near 0.94-0.98 m and localized motion around 0.52-0.70 m during part of P10. Shoot the controlled trihedral baseline next, after thermal stabilization, and interleave reference captures throughout the material run.

Recommended next capture

  1. Keep RX gain 24 dB, TX backoff 6 dB, HPF 0/0, all TX, 12 loops, bins 0-42, 10 ms period, 5 post frames.
  2. Let the radar reach a reasonably steady temperature; tonight's P10 bin-2 power changed +0.325 dB while mean RX temperature changed -3.50 °C.
  3. Place the trihedral at a tape-measured range, preferably well outside the coupling-dominated first bins, and keep the surrounding 0-2 m scene motionless.
  4. Take at least 10 baseline repeats, then interleave a baseline every material group. Preserve temperatures and exact CFG hashes.
  5. Before claiming bit-perfect transport in a PR, add an IWR-computed CRC32 (per frame and/or whole payload) and a monotonically increasing frame identifier.

Definitions and interpretation

dBFS: 10 log10(mean(|I+jQ|²) / 32768²). This is a digital FFT-output reference, not calibrated received power or RCS.

Fingerprint correlation: normalized complex correlation of the 12 TX/RX values at bin 2 after allowing a common complex scalar. It is sensitive to I/Q swaps and TX/RX/range indexing shifts.

P3 versus P10: the groups were taken about 12.6 minutes apart and at different thermal states; their level difference must not be attributed solely to frame period.
